codeReview.summary: The scoring engine implementation covers most requested behaviors, but there is a blocking defect in unknown-hardware scoring: speed normalization can exceed 1.0 and distort weighted composite scoring.

issues.description: _normalize_gen_tps_log() returns an unclamped ratio `log(1+gen_tps)/log(1+200)`. In unknown-hardware mode, _estimate_from_bandwidth_ratio() can produce gen_tps values above 200 (lines 262-266), which makes speed_score > 1.0 (e.g., 185 * 1000/546 ≈ 339 => log(340)/log(201) ≈ 1.10). This over-weights speed beyond configured intent weights and skews ranking.

Saved benchmark parsing defaults missing `memory_gb` to 0.0 (`saved.get("memory_gb", 0.0)`), and budget filtering later only checks `model.memory_gb <= budget` (line 437). Incomplete/malformed saved benchmark records can bypass memory-budget filtering and produce misleading recommendations.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Feature metadata references `cli-feature`, but the skill was not available to the worker at runtime; the worker proceeded without it and implemented production code before tests.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: features.json:619-622 shows `scoring-engine` uses `skillName: cli-feature`; transcript skeleton for session e40384a0-f338-467d-a037-901f67cd9801 line 268 shows `Error: Skill "cli-feature" not found`; lines 283-286 create `src/mlx_stack/core/scoring.py` before lines 300-303 create tests, while `.factory/skills/cli-feature/SKILL.md:65-67` requires tests before production code.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Shared schema expectations for saved benchmarks are inconsistent between scoring logic and the mission validation contract.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/mlx_stack/core/scoring.py:184-196 expects saved benchmark entries to include `memory_gb`; validation-contract.md:466-468 (VAL-BENCH-004) documents saved output fields as model ID, quant, prompt_tps, and gen_tps (no memory_gb).

summary: Reviewed handoff, transcript skeleton, and commit dfdb79e092315028e7e75c5e239ae6d9927f27b1 for feature `scoring-engine`. Implementation is close to spec, but unknown-hardware speed normalization can exceed the intended 0-1 range and distort weighted scoring, so this review fails with one blocking and one non-blocking issue.
